A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DreamText. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including reliable matching of relocated material.

before.justification: v3 reports original scene-text reconstruction and editing results, loss and hyperparameter ablations, balanced-supervision experiments, and generated examples.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds a warm-up-duration ablation and a human study of image quality and diversity.

M1.justification: The architecture, mask construction, loss terms, alternating optimization, and selected 25k-step warm-up remain. However, v3 uses α for both masked-diffusion weighting and cross-attention weighting; v4 replaces the former with γ without specifying its value or relationship to α. The PDFs do not establish whether this merely corrects notation or changes the objective's weighting.

E1.justification: SynthText, LAION-OCR, ICDAR13, and TextSeg remain the dataset coverage, with the same scene-text reconstruction and editing tasks. The added warm-up experiment and human assessment do not identify a new data domain, language, or input scenario.

E2.justification: The corresponding benchmark and qualitative comparisons retain SD-Inpainting, DiffSTE, MOSTEL, TextDiffuser, AnyText, and UDiffText. The new human study reuses UDiffText; no retained comparison adds or removes a comparator.

E3.justification: v4 adds experiments using 15k, 20k, 25k, and 30k warm-up durations. Appendix C introduces a 50-case human evaluation with four-image diversity assessments and a randomly selected image per case for quality assessment. Existing benchmark splits, training budgets, and automatic metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Table 4 directly tests sensitivity to warm-up duration, providing additional evidence for the existing 25k choice. The loss, α/β, and balanced-supervision ablations and attention visualizations are retained; v3 Table 4 becomes v4 Table 5.

E5.justification: v4 Figure 10 newly reports distributions of zero to five positive votes per query and highlights majority-consensus percentages, exposing agreement across five votes. Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests, or seed-based uncertainty for the model benchmarks.

E6.justification: Existing numerical tables and qualitative examples are retained. New Table 4 reports, for example, editing accuracy/FID of 0.891/13.24 at 30k warm-up versus 0.887/12.13 at 25k. Figure 10 adds majority-consensus percentages favoring DreamText versus UDiffText: 48% versus 29% for quality and 45% versus 31% for diversity.

T1.justification: No theorem, proof, or derivation is added, and the existing mathematical constructions remain. The unexplained α-to-γ substitution in the masked-loss definition leaves uncertainty about whether the complete objective is mathematically equivalent or now has independently weighted terms.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims concerning character-faithful synthesis, joint encoder/generator training, heuristic alternating optimization, balanced supervision, and superiority over existing methods. The added experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 3.1.4 refines the alignment explanation to emphasize whole-text visual/textual consistency. Section 4.3 adds an interpretation of the warm-up results as a trade-off between editing accuracy and image fidelity. Existing limitations and societal-impact discussions are preserved in Appendices G and H.

D1.justification: Figure 5 newly marks the image encoder as frozen and the auxiliary heads as trainable. Section 4.1.2 explicitly identifies the SD-v2.0 inpainting checkpoint, already indicated by v3's ablation setup. Hardware, training budgets, learning rate, and project link remain; the renamed masked-loss weight γ has no reported value.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to CA-GAN, Enhancing Object Coherence in Layout-to-Image Synthesis, and MagicFace without substantially revising the research positioning. It also removes the direct Break-a-scene citation from the masked-loss sentence while retaining that work's citation for cross-attention loss.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized wording and loss-explanation edits, updates author and affiliation information, and standardizes DreamText typography. It moves limitations and societal impact into the appendix and adds acknowledgments and an ethical statement. Most prose and the central narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds the warm-up table and human-study chart, updates Figure 5's training-status annotations, and relocates several existing displays. The earlier balanced-supervision table and appendix figures are renumbered, while their underlying content is retained.

improvement.justification: The new warm-up ablation provides direct support for the existing 25k-step choice, and Figure 5 improves training-status disclosure. The human study supplies additional subjective evidence, although case-source and rater-selection details are sparse. These limited gains outweigh the remaining documentation weaknesses, including the unexplained γ specification; the main benchmark findings and claims remain unchanged.
